items.duty_text: Organize and conduct an investigation of discrimination in employment for a period of one year, including testing local employers and sending out matched pairs of testers.
Organize and conduct an investigation of discrimination in housing accommodation services for a period of one year, including testing local housing accommodation providers.
Commence the housing discrimination investigation.
Make the climate survey available to all agencies for dissemination to agency employees.

observation.label: Awaiting an evidence detector
observation.note: No evidence detector for “data publication” yet.

items.deadline_text: Within 10 days after the commission initiates such investigation

items.duty_text: Consult with specified government officers, agencies, courts, and other designated bodies to obtain information about qualifying findings.
items.deadline_text: At least once every 30 days after the effective date

items.duty_text: Investigate all work performed and cases handled by the Police Department’s Equal Employment Opportunity Division during the specified period to determine whether they complied with the division’s purpose, mission, and protocols.
items.deadline_text: Section three takes effect 30 days after it becomes law

items.duty_text: Refer incidents of actual or perceived discrimination occurring during the investigation to the commission’s law enforcement bureau.

Include matched-pair testing in the housing discrimination investigation, using testers who apply for the same housing accommodations and present similar credit histories but different actual or perceived protected characteristics.

State findings of fact and conclusions of law and issue and cause to be served an order when the commission finds that a respondent engaged in an unlawful discriminatory practice or discriminatory harassment or violence.

Apply the highest hourly market-rate fee charged by attorneys of similar skill and experience within all jurisdictions located within the city when determining a reasonable hourly rate for a complainant’s attorney’s fee award based on the attorney’s hourly rate.
Foster mutual understanding and respect among all persons in the city.
Encourage equality of treatment and prevent discrimination against groups or their members.
Cooperate with governmental and nongovernmental agencies and organizations having like or kindred functions.
Make investigations and studies in human relations that will aid in effectuating its general purposes.
Appoint necessary employees and agents and assign them commission functions, powers, and duties, subject to nondelegation limits.

Receive, investigate, and decide complaints and initiate investigations concerning specified prejudice, disorder, and unlawful discrimination, with consultation before investigating alleged discrimination by city officials or agencies.
File complaints on its own motion alleging violations of the city’s human rights law.
Refer information indicating a possible discriminatory pattern or practice to the Corporation Counsel for a civil action.
Develop instructional courses and conduct ongoing public education concerning intergroup relations, bias-related harassment, and repeated hostile behavior.

Develop courses and conduct ongoing public education informing specified employers, employees, employment agencies, and job applicants about rights and responsibilities concerning unemployment discrimination.
Develop courses and conduct ongoing public education informing four-plus employers, employees, employment agencies, and job applicants about rights and responsibilities under section 8-2055.
Determine the form and manner of written notice concerning pregnancy, childbirth, and related medical-condition discrimination rights.
Make the assessment publicly available on its website.

observation.label: Awaiting an evidence detector
observation.note: No evidence detector for “data publication” yet.

items.duty_text: Develop a climate survey to assess awareness and knowledge of workplace sexual harassment policies and prevention at city agencies, including employee experience with and knowledge of reporting, and include optional questions regarding race, ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, and age.

observation.label: Awaiting an evidence detector
observation.note: No evidence detector for “data publication” yet.

items.duty_text: Use the climate survey to assess each agency on the enumerated sexual-harassment-awareness, reporting, safety, prevention, investigation, and response factors.
Create a model lactation policy and a model lactation space request form in collaboration with the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene.
Make the model lactation policy and model lactation space request form available on its website.

observation.label: Awaiting an evidence detector
observation.note: No evidence detector for “data publication” yet.

items.duty_text: Engage in outreach and education regarding the rights of current and prospective employees and the responsibilities of employers established by the local law, directed at public and private employers and the general public.
Develop and disseminate a written notice describing protections related to lawful source of income discrimination.
Make the written notice available to the Department of Social Services for use under § 21-141.1.
Include informational resources on age discrimination as part of its regular outreach and education efforts.

Create an age-discrimination poster describing age discrimination, providing examples of prohibited conduct, explaining how to file a complaint, and including information on additional age-discrimination resources.
Make additional resources on age discrimination available on the commission’s website.

observation.label: Awaiting an evidence detector
observation.note: No evidence detector for “data publication” yet.

items.duty_text: For a period of three years, organize and conduct no fewer than five investigations of age discrimination in the workplace per year, using pairs of testers to investigate specified employers, labor organizations, employment agencies, and their employees or agents.
Include matched-pair tester applications for the same job using similar credentials but different actual or perceived ages, with at least one tester presenting as above age 50, in each investigation.
Commence the investigation of age discrimination in the workplace.
Refer incidents of actual or perceived discrimination occurring during the investigation to the commission’s law enforcement bureau.
Initiate its own investigation of qualifying past conduct by a current or former police department employee.
Determine what constitutes an act exhibiting prejudice, intolerance or bigotry, or unlawful discrimination, for purposes of initiating an investigation.
Determine what constitutes a qualifying finding that a current or former police department employee engaged in such an act for purposes of initiating an investigation.
Determine which types of qualifying past official conduct to investigate based on the employee’s professional rank and assigned roles.
Investigate qualifying past official conduct from the employee’s date of hire through the applicable end date.
Ensure that a designated third party and its personnel keep investigation information confidential and do not disclose it outside the commission.
Initiate and undertake investigations in accordance with the investigation, recordkeeping, and charter requirements applicable to investigations initiated by the commission on its own.

The commission shall not have jurisdiction over complaints filed more than one year after the alleged unlawful discriminatory practice or act of discriminatory harassment or violence occurred, except that it shall have jurisdiction over gender-based harassment claims filed within three years after the alleged harassing conduct occurred.

items.duty_text: Refer incidents of actual or perceived discrimination occurring during the investigation to the commission’s law enforcement bureau.

Include matched-pair testing in the housing discrimination investigation, using testers who apply for the same housing accommodations and present similar credit histories but different actual or perceived protected characteristics.

State findings of fact and conclusions of law and issue and cause to be served an order when the commission finds that a respondent engaged in an unlawful discriminatory practice or discriminatory harassment or violence.

Apply the highest hourly market-rate fee charged by attorneys of similar skill and experience within all jurisdictions located within the city when determining a reasonable hourly rate for a complainant’s attorney’s fee award based on the attorney’s hourly rate.
Foster mutual understanding and respect among all persons in the city.
Encourage equality of treatment and prevent discrimination against groups or their members.
Cooperate with governmental and nongovernmental agencies and organizations having like or kindred functions.
Make investigations and studies in human relations that will aid in effectuating its general purposes.
Appoint necessary employees and agents and assign them commission functions, powers, and duties, subject to nondelegation limits.

Receive, investigate, and decide complaints and initiate investigations concerning specified prejudice, disorder, and unlawful discrimination, with consultation before investigating alleged discrimination by city officials or agencies.
File complaints on its own motion alleging violations of the city’s human rights law.
Refer information indicating a possible discriminatory pattern or practice to the Corporation Counsel for a civil action.
Develop instructional courses and conduct ongoing public education concerning intergroup relations, bias-related harassment, and repeated hostile behavior.

Develop courses and conduct ongoing public education informing specified employers, employees, employment agencies, and job applicants about rights and responsibilities concerning unemployment discrimination.
Develop courses and conduct ongoing public education informing four-plus employers, employees, employment agencies, and job applicants about rights and responsibilities under section 8-2055.
Determine the form and manner of written notice concerning pregnancy, childbirth, and related medical-condition discrimination rights.
Make the assessment publicly available on its website.

items.duty_text: Develop a climate survey to assess awareness and knowledge of workplace sexual harassment policies and prevention at city agencies, including employee experience with and knowledge of reporting, and include optional questions regarding race, ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, and age.

observation.label: Awaiting an evidence detector

items.duty_text: Use the climate survey to assess each agency on the enumerated sexual-harassment-awareness, reporting, safety, prevention, investigation, and response factors.
Create a model lactation policy and a model lactation space request form in collaboration with the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene.
Make the model lactation policy and model lactation space request form available on its website.

observation.label: Awaiting an evidence detector
observation.note: No evidence detector for “data publication” yet.

items.duty_text: Engage in outreach and education regarding the rights of current and prospective employees and the responsibilities of employers established by the local law, directed at public and private employers and the general public.
Develop and disseminate a written notice describing protections related to lawful source of income discrimination.
Make the written notice available to the Department of Social Services for use under § 21-141.1.
Include informational resources on age discrimination as part of its regular outreach and education efforts.

Create an age-discrimination poster describing age discrimination, providing examples of prohibited conduct, explaining how to file a complaint, and including information on additional age-discrimination resources.
Make additional resources on age discrimination available on the commission’s website.

observation.label: Awaiting an evidence detector
observation.note: No evidence detector for “data publication” yet.

items.duty_text: For a period of three years, organize and conduct no fewer than five investigations of age discrimination in the workplace per year, using pairs of testers to investigate specified employers, labor organizations, employment agencies, and their employees or agents.
Include matched-pair tester applications for the same job using similar credentials but different actual or perceived ages, with at least one tester presenting as above age 50, in each investigation.
Commence the investigation of age discrimination in the workplace.
Refer incidents of actual or perceived discrimination occurring during the investigation to the commission’s law enforcement bureau.
Initiate its own investigation of qualifying past conduct by a current or former police department employee.
Determine what constitutes an act exhibiting prejudice, intolerance or bigotry, or unlawful discrimination, for purposes of initiating an investigation.
Determine what constitutes a qualifying finding that a current or former police department employee engaged in such an act for purposes of initiating an investigation.
Determine which types of qualifying past official conduct to investigate based on the employee’s professional rank and assigned roles.
Investigate qualifying past official conduct from the employee’s date of hire through the applicable end date.
Ensure that a designated third party and its personnel keep investigation information confidential and do not disclose it outside the commission.
Initiate and undertake investigations in accordance with the investigation, recordkeeping, and charter requirements applicable to investigations initiated by the commission on its own.

The commission shall not have jurisdiction over complaints filed more than one year after the alleged unlawful discriminatory practice or act of discriminatory harassment or violence occurred, except that it shall have jurisdiction over gender-based harassment claims filed within three years after the alleged harassing conduct occurred.
